record.paper_title: Global results on rational systems in the plane, part 1
record.original_question: For the system x_{n+1} = (b1 x_n + g1 y_n)/(1 + y_n), y_{n+1} = (b2 x_n + g2 y_n)/(1 + x_n), with positive parameters and nonnegative initial conditions not both zero, determine whether the system has prime period-two solutions. If prime period-two solutions exist, determine their global character; if they do not exist, prove their absence and give the corresponding global behavior.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the planar system of rational difference equations
  x_{n+1} = (b_1 x_n + g_1 y_n)/(1 + y_n),
  y_{n+1} = (b_2 x_n + g_2 y_n)/(1 + x_n),
for n = 0, 1, 2, ..., where the parameters b_1, g_1, b_2, g_2 are positive real numbers and the initial conditions (x_0, y_0) are nonnegative real numbers, not both zero (so that the iteration is well defined and remains in the nonnegative quadrant).

A solution {(x_n, y_n)} is called a prime period-two solution if there exist two distinct points P, Q in the nonnegative quadrant such that (x_n, y_n) = P for n even and (x_n, y_n) = Q for n odd (or vice versa), and no period-one (equilibrium) reduction holds.

Tasks:
1. Determine, in terms of the parameters (b_1, g_1, b_2, g_2), exactly when the system admits a prime period-two solution.
2. If prime period-two solutions exist, describe them explicitly and determine their global character (local and global stability, basin of attraction, and the long-term behavior of all admissible solutions).
3. If no prime period-two solutions exist, prove their nonexistence and describe the global behavior (boundedness, convergence to equilibria, etc.) of all admissible solutions.
